t: Minimum Number of Flips to Make Binary Grid Palindromic II
o: Cells partition into orbits under the reflections (i ↔ n−1−i, j ↔ m−1−j). Orbits of size 4 must become uniform (cost = min(#1s, #0s)); orbit pairs on the middle row/column of size 2 must become equal (cost = min(c, 2−c)); a center cell is free. After these choices, the total count of 1s must be ≡ 0 (mod 4). Track how many 1s result and adjust using the flexibility of certain groups at extra cost.
k: Size-4 orbits with exactly 2 ones can switch 0000↔1111 at zero extra cost (Δones = ±4... actually ±2 mod 4 = 2); orbits with 1 or 3 ones cost +2 to switch; size-2 orbits with c=1 can pick 00 or 11 at the same cost (free toggle of ones parity-by-2); size-2 with c=0 or 2 toggles at +2 cost.
A lone center cell can be flipped at +1 cost, changing ones count by 1 — fixes residues 1 and 3.
Residue 2 needs a free toggle (mixed pair or balanced quad) or a +2 toggle (1/3-quad or uniform pair).

a.n: Approach 1: Orbit grouping with residue repair
a.i: First make every orbit uniform at minimal cost, accumulating the resulting ones count. Then repair the mod-4 residue using the cheapest available flexibility: center flip (+1), free toggles (+0), or expensive toggles (+2).
s: For each orbit: size 4 → base += min(c, 4−c), ones += (c ≥ 2 ? 4 : 0), flag quad2 if c==2, quad13 if c∈{1,3}. Size 2 → base += min(c, 2−c), ones += (c==1 ? 0 : c), flag mixedFree if c==1 else pairToggle. Size 1 → ones += cell, center = true.
If r == 0 return base; if r == 2: return base if (mixedFree or quad2), base+2 if (quad13 or pairToggle), else -1; if center exists return base+1; else -1.
a.t: O(n·m) — each cell examined a constant number of times through its orbit

a.n: Approach 2: Direct four-cell iteration without sets
a.i: Handle the three orbit shapes with explicit index arithmetic instead of set deduplication — slightly faster and avoids hashing, same logic.
s: Quad case: i < n−1−i and j < m−1−j → four distinct cells.
Pair cases: exactly one of the two equalities holds → two distinct cells.
Center: both equalities hold → single cell.
a.t: O(n·m) — quarter-grid iteration with constant work per orbit

w: Carefully verify the residue-repair table against all three examples (3, 2, 2). The subtle points: a mixed middle pair contributes exactly one 1 whichever way you orient it is WRONG — it can be 00 or 11 at equal cost, hence a free ±2 toggle; and the center flip is the only ±1 lever. Test tiny grids ([[1]], [[1],[1]]) explicitly. Follow-up: version I (only palindromic, no mod-4) is just the base computation.
